newsitem.title: USA: Wellman says strike ends at Irish plant.
newsitem.headline: Wellman says strike ends at Irish plant.

text.p: Wellman Inc said on Wednesday a labor dispute ended at its fiber production facility in Mullagh, Ireland.
Production at the facility, which has been idle for the past 12 weeks, was restarted today.
The striking workers left their jobs in mid-July to protest the redeployment of 35 workers to other departments at the facility and work practice changes implemented in early June, the company said.

Wellman said the changes, which stemmed from the installation of new production equipment at the facility in 1995, were implemented after two years of negotiations and approval by the Irish Labour Court.
The strikers voted by 6 to 1 to end the dispute after receiving an invitation by the local management to return to work today with the rest of the workforce.
The plant is operating under the company's original, Labour Court-endorsed staffing and work practice proposals.
Wellman said 260 workers took part in the strike, representing one of the four unions at the facility. The fiber plant employs 490 workers, Wellman said.
